core.title: Give every plan-declared route and exposed journey a bound e2e proof at its canonical location
core.given: The plan declares a route (within its route group) or an exposed journey (new or existing, changed or not)
core.when: you change code or tests, or the stack's topology check reports a finding of this rule
core.then: Ensure it has an e2e test at its canonical e2e location (per the profile's e2e location pattern) carrying a test URN naming a plan-declared feature AND an acceptance binding for an acceptance declared by a plan artifact; a file at the location lacking either does not count.
prefer: Add the test at exactly the path the finding names.
Copy feature and acceptance ids from the plan's declarations.
avoid: Ad-hoc e2e locations found only by searching.
Undeclared features in test URNs; acceptance ids no plan artifact declares; empty files at the canonical location.
An acceptance binding line in a browser-level journey spec (a sibling rule forbids it there).
unless: Exposed journey whose declared surfaces include `frontend`: a browser-level e2e spec substitutes when it is bound to the same subject — the journey, or the route's user/system flow — via the profile's subject bindings and carries a valid browser-test URN for that same subject (the user/system-flow-subject e2e or journey-subject smoke test-identity URN from the profile) instead of an acceptance binding line.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned (the stack-wide exclusion list from the profile; the checker owns the exact classification).
core.why: One behaviour, one end-to-end proof at a location derived from the plan: a missing proof is found by path, not by searching.
evidence: For every plan-declared route, an e2e test exists at its canonical e2e location.

For every exposed journey, an e2e test exists at its canonical location, or (frontend surface) a browser-level spec bound to the same subject carries a valid user/system-flow-subject e2e or journey-subject smoke test URN for it.
Each canonical e2e test relied on as the proof carries a test URN for a plan-declared feature and an acceptance binding declared by a plan artifact.
No browser-level journey spec contains an acceptance binding line.
The topology check reports no finding of this rule.
verification: Check every plan-declared route and exposed journey, changed or not: the check is driven by the plan's declarations, not by the diff; change facts are only an early trigger.

A file at the canonical e2e location without both a test URN naming a declared feature and a plan-artifact-declared acceptance binding is a finding — unconditionally for routes and non-frontend exposed journeys; for frontend exposed journeys only when no qualifying browser-spec substitute exists.

Browser-spec substitution applies only to exposed journeys whose declared surfaces include `frontend`; its qualifications — subject binding via the profile's subject-binding syntaxes and a valid browser-test URN for that same subject (the user/system-flow-subject e2e or journey-subject smoke test-identity shape from the profile) — are evaluated only when the spec is relied on as the substitute, i.e. no qualifying canonical e2e test exists at the canonical location. Extra browser specs alongside a qualifying canonical test are not judged by this rule.

The observer must parse the plan's declared routes, exposed journeys and their surfaces, declared features and plan-declared acceptances, and the e2e tests' URNs, acceptance bindings and subject bindings (needs_new_observer).
Canonical locations and root paths resolve from the profile: the e2e location pattern and the plan and e2e roots (declared in the repository's root/config declaration).
Browser-level specs carry their identity as a browser-test URN, never as an acceptance binding line; a sibling rule forbids that line on journey specs.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned; the exact exclusion classification is the one stack-wide list owned by the profile and the checker, not an extra per-rule list.
Severity 3, disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding.

fires: A plan-declared route — new or long-existing and untouched — has no e2e test at its canonical e2e location.
An exposed journey has no e2e test at its canonical location, and (if its declared surfaces include `frontend`) no qualifying browser-level spec either.

For a route, a non-frontend exposed journey, or a frontend exposed journey with no qualifying browser substitute: the e2e test at the canonical location carries no test URN, or its URN names a feature the plan does not declare.

For a route, a non-frontend exposed journey, or a frontend exposed journey with no qualifying browser substitute: the e2e test at the canonical location has no acceptance binding, or binds an acceptance no plan artifact declares.

A browser-level spec is the only proof relied on for a frontend exposed journey (no qualifying canonical test) and it lacks a subject binding, is bound to a different subject than its URN, or lacks a valid user/system-flow-subject e2e or journey-subject smoke test URN for that subject.
A browser-level spec is the only proof relied on for an exposed journey whose surfaces do not include `frontend`.
doesNotFire: Files under vendored or generated trees.
Unit and acceptance tests under the test root unrelated to any declared route or exposed journey.

A frontend exposed journey proven by a browser-level spec bound to the route's user/system flow or to the journey and carrying a valid user/system-flow-subject e2e or journey-subject smoke test URN for that same subject — even if a nonqualifying canonical test also exists at the canonical location.

A browser-level spec not relied on as the substitute because the route or journey already has a qualifying canonical e2e test at its canonical location (this rule does not judge such extra browser specs).

profileRequirements.meaning: Test-identity URN shape by which the canonical e2e test identifies the feature and acceptance it proves.
Test-identity URN shape of a browser-level e2e test whose subject is a user/system flow (the route's user/system flow); not the user/system flow artifact's own URN.
Test-identity URN shape of a browser-level smoke test whose subject is a journey; not the smoke-acceptance artifact's own URN.
URN shape of the acceptance artifact referenced by the binding line.
Syntax by which the canonical e2e test binds the acceptance it proves.
Syntax by which a browser-level spec binds itself to the route's user/system flow.
Syntax by which a browser-level spec binds itself to the journey.
Name patterns of the stack's e2e test kinds: the canonical tests at their locations and the browser-level specs.
Vendored and generated trees that are never scanned.

neutralityNotes: ATDD-Bun's route grouping ('flow router') has no cross-stack name in the closed vocabulary; the core says 'route (within its route group)' and the grouping plus concrete paths live in layout.e2e_location. The browser-level substitute (Playwright in Bun) is kept as a neutral mechanism: the core states the qualification (same subject binding, a valid browser-test URN for that subject, no acceptance line) and the profile supplies the spec kind (suffix.e2e_test), the subject bindings (urn.binding.user-system-flow / urn.binding.journey) and the browser-test identity URNs (proposed test-identity keys urn.test_kinds#user_system_flow_e2e_test and urn.test_kinds#journey_smoke_test — artifact URN keys urn.user-system-flow and urn.smoke_acceptance stay reserved for their artifact identities); the `…` suffix of E2E/SMOKE test URNs is kept verbatim because the source does not define it further. The canonical e2e test's own URN shape also had no fitting key and is proposed as urn.test_kinds#e2e_test. 'frontend' is kept as a plan-declared surface value (plan vocabulary, not a stack name). Validator/finding ids (atdd_topology, atdd-bun.topology.e2e-location), the sibling-rule id (tester.htmx.journey-no-acceptance-marker) and the config file/key names (atdd-bun.yaml topology keys) are realization details: the core's verification names the checks generically and takes resolved roots from the profile.
